name: Canis Minor
introduction: is the Little Dog, the smaller of Orion’s two hunting dogs. It consists of little more than two stars, but one of them is Procyon, which forms the Winter Triangle together with Betelgeuse and Sirius. It is best seen on northern winter evenings.

sections.title: What makes it special
paragraphs: [Procyon](hip:37279), only 11 light-years away, is one of our nearest bright neighbors. Its name means “before the dog”, because it rises shortly before Sirius, the Dog Star. Like Sirius, it has a white dwarf companion, [Procyon B](id:10pc-0032), discovered in 1896.

Nearby in space lies [Luyten’s Star](id:10pc-0053), a red dwarf about 12 light-years away with a planet in its habitable zone. In 2017, a radio message carrying music and greetings was sent toward it.

sections.title: Notable stars
paragraphs: [Gomeisa](hip:36188), the second star, is a hot blue-white star about 160 light-years away, surrounded by a disk of gas thrown off by its rapid rotation.
Procyon itself is a slightly evolved star, larger and brighter than the Sun, beginning to swell as it uses up the hydrogen in its core.

sections.title: Beyond the stars
paragraphs: Canis Minor contains no Messier objects, but its location on the edge of the Milky Way places it next to Monoceros, with its rich star fields and nebulae.
